sites.n: Ichnia 6th MoD arsenal fire and explosions

sites.kf: MVS: fire and explosions at the 6th arsenal of the Ministry of Defence near Ichnia; residents of Ichnia and 30 nearby settlements within a 16 km zone evacuated; 163 patients moved from the central district hospital; 2,277 people (256 children) housed in 11 evacuation points; more than 1,000 personnel and 212 vehicles deployed (DSNS 257 people, 74 vehicles); no information on dead or injured.

sites.kf: HZS ČR: 16 Oct 2014, explosions of two munitions stores in the Military Technical Institute area at Vlachovice-Vrbětice (store no. 16 first); the joint intervention of the security forces ended on 13 Oct 2020 at 19:00 after almost six years. Czech government (18 Apr 2021): reasonable suspicion of involvement of Russian GRU officers; 18 Russian embassy staff expelled; the government described it as an act in which two Czech citizens died.

cas: Displaced: more than 700 families (US State Dept, reported)

US State Dept (2012): US-funded clean-up removed about 3,085 t of UXO and 146,500 munitions and cleared 257 acres.

Serbian government: UNDP donation for clearance of the site.

sites.n: Stadtallendorf former explosives factories (DAG and WASAG)
sites.ty: Former Third Reich explosives works; remediation by state of Hessen (HIM GmbH) · TNT and other explosives residues, PAH; PFT
sites.st: remediation largely complete; groundwater hydraulically secured
sites.kf: Hessen: described as Europe's largest armament legacy site; two former explosives works (DAG, WASAG); the DAG site (~600 ha) contains a waterworks supplying central Hesse; soil and groundwater contaminated with TNT, PAH and others; 150-200 plots needing remediation; work began May 1997 and the DAG site was finished at the end of 2002 except outer areas; 'Tri-Halde' (85,000 t sludge) remediated over 18 months from 2003; PFT from a fire found in groundwater; 1990 settlement of DM 25 million with IVG.

src.t: Hessian Ministry (landwirtschaft.hessen.de), 'Altlastensanierung' (Stadtallendorf and Hessisch Lichtenau armament sites)

sites.ty: Former Third Reich TNT works; remediation by state of Hessen · TNT, PAH
sites.st: surface soil remediation complete 2009; hydraulic containment and monitoring continue
sites.kf: Hessen: about 233 ha and about 100 plots; TNT and PAH; soil remediation from 1998, surface soil remediation ended 2009; hydraulic groundwater containment and monitoring continue. RP Kassel: about 20 km SE of Kassel; one of the largest explosives factories of the Third Reich, mainly TNT.

sites.ty: Former UKAEA fast-reactor and reprocessing site; NDA-funded beach monitoring under SEPA regulation · radioactive particles (Cs-137) from fuel reprocessing

sites.n: HM Naval Base Clyde (Faslane and Coulport)
sites.ty: Royal Navy submarine base and nuclear-weapons storage/loading; SEPA via MoU with the Defence Nuclear Safety Regulator · radioactive discharges and waste; nuclear safety events
sites.kf: SEPA (10 Dec 2025): EASR 2018 is disapplied for defence premises and applied through an MoU (2022) reviewed with DNSR; 2024 public doses were 0.5% of the dose limit; discharges well within agreed limits; MoD nearing completion of a Nuclear Support Hub to handle all radioactive waste at Faslane.

sites.n: Yunkom (Yunyi Komunar) mine - 1979 'Klivazh' underground nuclear explosion
sites.ty: flooded coal mine with Soviet peaceful nuclear explosion cavity
sites.kf: MVS: in 1979 an experimental underground nuclear explosion of 300 t yield was carried out at about 900 m depth in the 'Young Communard' mine, creating the 'Klivazh' capsule containing radionuclides (Cs, Sr, Pu); pumping stopped in April 2018 and the mine is flooding, threatening groundwater.
